title: Smoothing and premelting correction of heat capacity data
action: Using the raw heat capacity data, temperature increments, phase transition data, and cryoscopic constants, perform premelting corrections and generate smoothed C_s(T) curves for all crystalline and liquid phases of the four compounds. For liquid phases, use the provided cubic polynomial coefficients to produce smooth values. The smoothed curves are required for the subsequent numerical integration.
description: Produce smoothed heat capacity curves per phase as intermediate input for integration.

title: Compute condensed phase thermodynamic functions
action: Numerically integrate the smoothed C_s(T) curves (with Debye function extrapolation below 10 K) and incorporate phase transition enthalpies and triple-point corrections. Compute at the same selected temperatures as in the published condensed-phase table the five thermodynamic quantities: -{G_s(T)-H°(0)}/T, {H_s(T)-H°(0)}/T, {H_s(T)-H°(0)}, S_s, and C_s for all phases of all four compounds. Output a CSV file with columns: compound, phase, T (K), neg_Gs_over_T (cal_th K⁻¹ mol⁻¹), Hs_over_T (cal_th K⁻¹ mol⁻¹), Hs (cal_th mol⁻¹), Ss (cal_th K⁻¹ mol⁻¹), Cs (cal_th K⁻¹ mol⁻¹).
description: One row per (compound, phase, temperature) with the five thermodynamic quantities in cal_th units.
output_schema: columns: compound, phase, T (K), neg_Gs_over_T (cal_th K^-1 mol^-1), Hs_over_T (cal_th K^-1 mol^-1), Hs (cal_th mol^-1), Ss (cal_th K^-1 mol^-1), Cs (cal_th K^-1 mol^-1)

title: Compute ideal gas entropies at 298.15 K
action: Using the liquid entropy S_s(l) at 298.15 K from the condensed-phase table and the provided vaporization data (ΔH_vap, ΔS_vap, (S_ideal – S_s) correction, R ln(p/atm)), compute the standard ideal gas entropy S°(298.15 K) for all four compounds. Output a CSV file with columns: compound, S_ideal_298.15 (cal_th K⁻¹ mol⁻¹).
description: One row per compound with the computed S°(298.15 K) in cal_th K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.

title: Compute ideal gas thermodynamic functions and formation properties for acrylonitrile
action: Using the provided fundamental vibrational wavenumbers, moments of inertia, and the rigid-rotator harmonic-oscillator approximation, compute the ideal gas thermodynamic functions (Gibbs energy function, enthalpy function, entropy, heat capacity) for acrylonitrile at temperatures up to 1000 K. Then, using the provided enthalpy of combustion, literature enthalpies of formation of CO₂(g) and H₂O(l), and the provided JANAF elemental data, compute the enthalpy of formation, Gibbs energy of formation, and log₁₀ equilibrium constant of formation. Output a CSV file with columns: T, neg_G_over_T, H_over_T, S, Cp, ΔH_f°, ΔG_f°, log_K_f.
description: One row per temperature T (K) with columns: T, neg_G_over_T, H_over_T, S, Cp, ΔH_f°, ΔG_f°, log_K_f (units cal_th K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, cal_th mol⁻¹, kcal_th mol⁻¹).
output_schema: columns: T, neg_G_over_T, H_over_T, S, Cp, ΔH_f°, ΔG_f°, log_K_f
